#!/bin/bash
# Build a project subtree in a scratch directory so the repo stays clean.
#
# The checked-in host tools (elf2char/createimage/generateMapping) are mode
# 644 in git and the Makefile hard-codes a cross prefix that does not exist in
# this container, so we copy the tree out and fix both there.  gcc >= 10 also
# defaults to -fno-common, which trips over the generated user_programs.h; the
# original lab toolchain was older, hence -fcommon.
#
# usage: agent_tests/build.sh <ProjectDir> [make target...]
set -u

PROJ="$1"; shift
SRC="/workspace/$PROJ"
DST="/tmp/b/$(echo "$PROJ" | cut -c1-8)"

[ -d "$SRC" ] || { echo "no such project: $SRC"; exit 2; }

rm -rf "$DST"
mkdir -p /tmp/b
cp -a "$SRC" "$DST" || exit 2
chmod +x "$DST"/elf2char "$DST"/createimage "$DST"/generateMapping 2>/dev/null

sed -i 's/^CROSS_PREFIX = .*/CROSS_PREFIX = riscv64-linux-gnu-/' "$DST/Makefile"
sed -i 's/^\(CFLAGS = .*\)$/\1 -fcommon/' "$DST/Makefile"
sed -i 's/^\(USER_CFLAGS = .*\)$/\1 -fcommon/' "$DST/Makefile"

cd "$DST" || exit 2
timeout 1200 make "${@:-main}" 2>&1
build.sh
hostshim

p2b_sched_test.c
p3_proc_test.c

#!/bin/bash
# Host-side functional tests for the kernel subsystems implemented in this repo.
#
# Kernel code is compiled natively (with small shims under hostshim/ standing in
# for the RISC-V specific headers) and driven directly, so the scheduling,
# synchronisation, IPC and file-system logic can be executed and asserted on
# without a board or an emulator.
set -u

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
ROOT=$(pwd)
SHIM="$ROOT/agent_tests/hostshim"
OUT=$(mktemp -d)
fail=0

run_case() {
    local name=$1; shift
    if ! gcc -g -O0 -o "$OUT/$name" "$@" 2>"$OUT/$name.log"; then
        echo "[$name] COMPILE FAILED"
        sed -n '1,40p' "$OUT/$name.log"
        fail=1
        return
    fi
    if ! timeout 60 "$OUT/$name"; then
        echo "[$name] RUN FAILED"
        fail=1
    fi
}

P2A="$ROOT/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1"
run_case p2a_sched \
    "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2a_sched_test.c" \
    "$P2A/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P2A/kernel/locking/lock.c" \
    -I"$SHIM" -I"$P2A/include" -I"$P2A/drivers" -I"$P2A/arch/riscv/include"

# get_ticks() reads the RISC-V `time` CSR, which the host cannot execute.  Swap
# just that one read for a counter the test drives; timer_check() -- the code
# actually under test -- is compiled verbatim.
host_time_c() {
    python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
import sys
src = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
asm = '''    __asm__ __volatile__(
        "rdtime %0"
        : "=r"(time_elapsed));'''
assert asm in src, "get_ticks() no longer looks the way the test expects"
src = src.replace(asm, "    time_elapsed = host_get_ticks();")
src = "extern unsigned long host_get_ticks(void);\n" + src
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(src)
PY
}

P2B="$ROOT/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2b_sched_test.c" ]; then
    host_time_c "$P2B/kernel/sched/time.c" "$OUT/p2b_time.c"
    run_case p2b_sched \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2b_sched_test.c" \
        "$P2B/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P2B/kernel/locking/lock.c" \
        "$P2B/kernel/locking/futex.c" "$P2B/kernel/locking/binsem.c" \
        "$OUT/p2b_time.c" \
atomic.h
type.h

content.text:
I've completed a deep review of the P4 shared-memory implementation, including building a host harness that compiles the real `mm.c` and executes `shm_page_get`/`shm_page_dt`/`free_process_user_page` against the exact `test/consensus.c` sequence plus randomized invariant fuzzing (refcount == number of live mappings, no live PTE to a freed frame, no multi-mapped non-shm frame, no frame/pgdir/disk-slot leaks) — including under memory pressure that forces eviction. The core refcounting, first-use allocation, VA selection, U|R|W flags, and the `free_process_user_page` "shared page must not be freed as private" path all hold up.

Two real defects remain:

findings.title: shm_page_dt() walks the page table for an unvalidated user pointer, and find_pte() mistakes the kernel megapage leaf for a table pointer
findings.detail:
shm_page_dt() takes `addr` straight from a0 of the SYSCALL_SHMPDT trap (init/main.c:146 -> syscall.c:10) and passes it to find_pte() with no range check at all. find_pte() (mm.c:189-205) only tests _PAGE_PRESENT at levels 2 and 1; it never tests R/W/X, so it cannot tell a pointer entry from a megapage leaf.

Every user page table contains the kernel window entry copied verbatim by init_page_table() (mm.c:255: `pgdir_kva[0x101] = kernel_pgdir_kva[0x101]`). boot.c installs that entry as a *pointer* (V only) to a second-level table whose entries 0x80..0xFF are 2 MB *leaves* (arch/riscv/kernel/boot.c:24-42). So for a kernel-half address the walk succeeds at level 2, then treats a 2 MB leaf as a table pointer and returns a pointer into ordinary kernel memory.

Worked example for addr = 0xffffffc050400000 (kernel image base): VPN2 = 0x101 -> present pointer to PGDIR_PA+0x1000; VPN1 = 0x82 -> a 2 MB leaf with PFN 0x50400; find_pte does `table = pa2kva(0x50400000)`; VPN0 = 0 -> it returns (PTE*)0xffffffc050400000, i.e. the first 8 bytes of the kernel image reinterpreted as a leaf PTE.

shm_page_dt then does `get_attribute(*pte, _PAGE_PRESENT)` on that kernel word. RISC-V 32-bit instructions have bits[1:0] == 0b11, so bit 0 is set for most kernel code words and the "present" test passes. It then computes `pa = get_pa(*pte)` from kernel code bytes and scans shm_page[]; if that bogus pa happens to equal a live segment's pa it executes `*pte = 0` (mm.c:382), zeroing a word of kernel text/data, and additionally decrements a refcount that this process never incremented — which can drop the count to zero and free a frame that other processes still have mapped.

Note the author guarded exactly this in handle_page_fault (mm.c:399 rejects stval >= 1<<38 before touching the page table); shm_page_dt is the one user-reachable path into the walkers that has no such guard. The identical code exists at Project5-Device_Driver/kernel/mm/mm.c:388 and in the in-progress Project6 copy.
findings.why_wrong: A user program can hand any 64-bit value to sys_shmpage_dt (a stale or uninitialised pointer is enough - consensus.c itself keeps using `vars` after detaching it). The kernel must never derive a PTE pointer from an unvalidated user address, and a page-table walker must stop when an intermediate entry has R/W/X set instead of following its PFN as if it were a next-level table. Here the guaranteed effect is a wild kernel read, and the possible effect is a kernel-memory write plus corruption of the shared-segment refcount, which then frees a page other processes still map.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject non-user addresses at the top of shm_page_dt, mirroring handle_page_fault: `if (addr >= (1lu << (VPN2_SHIFT + PPN_BITS - 1))) return;` (or, tighter, require SHM_VA_BEGIN <= addr < SHM_VA_END). Additionally harden find_pte/walk_pgdir to return NULL when an intermediate entry is a leaf, e.g. inside the level loop: `if (get_attribute(*entry, _PAGE_READ | _PAGE_WRITE | _PAGE_EXEC)) return NULL;`.

findings.title: Shared segments are indexed by key % SHM_PAGE_NUM without storing the key, so distinct keys alias onto one segment
findings.detail:
shm_page_get() selects the segment with `shm_page_t *page = &shm_page[(uint32_t)key % SHM_PAGE_NUM];` (SHM_PAGE_NUM == 100, include/os/mm.h:79) and the shm_page_t slot only holds `{count, pa}` — the key is never recorded and never compared. Consequently any two keys congruent modulo 100 resolve to the same slot.

Concretely: process A calls sys_shmpage_get(1) -> slot 1, count becomes 1, backed by frame X. Process B then calls sys_shmpage_get(101), which is an unrelated segment as far as B is concerned. Because slot 1 already has count > 0, the `if (page->count == 0)` branch at mm.c:339 is skipped, no new frame is allocated, and B is handed a mapping of A's frame X with count going to 2. The two processes now silently read and write each other's memory, and each one's shm_page_dt/exit decrements the other's refcount.

The reverse aliasing also breaks isolation in the other direction: if A detaches first, B's segment survives only because A's count was pooled with B's; if both detach, the frame is freed once for what the callers believe are two independent segments.

The same code is at Project5-Device_Driver/kernel/mm/mm.c:354. The lab's own test only uses key 42 (test/consensus.c:10), so this does not show up in the shipped test, but sys_shmpage_get(int key) is a general API with no documented key range.
findings.why_wrong: A shared-memory key namespace must map distinct keys to distinct segments (or explicitly reject out-of-range keys). Hashing the key into a fixed table while discarding it makes collisions silently return the wrong segment instead of a new one, which breaks address-space isolation between unrelated processes and makes the refcount for one segment be driven by attaches/detaches of another.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a key field to the slot and compare it: search shm_page[] for an entry with `count > 0 && key_of[i] == key`, else claim a slot with `count == 0`, record `key_of[i] = key`, and return 0 when the table is full. If changing shm_page_t is not desired, at minimum reject keys outside [0, SHM_PAGE_NUM) (`if ((unsigned)key >= SHM_PAGE_NUM) return 0;`) so an aliased key fails loudly instead of silently sharing another segment.
